Name: Sarah
Age: 40
Gender: Female
Admission date: [Date]
Discharge date: [Date]
Reason for Admission: COVID-19 with symptoms of rhinorrhea, hyposmia, and ageusia

Hospital Course:
Sarah was admitted to the hospital with positive COVID-19 test results and mild symptoms of rhinorrhea, hyposmia, and ageusia. During her stay, she was treated with hydroxychloroquine and azithromycin, and her symptoms gradually improved. After three consecutive COVID-19 RT-PCR tests came back negative, she was discharged from the hospital in stable condition.

Follow-Up Care:
Sarah visited the Otolaryngology clinic one month after her discharge. She reported that her olfactory and gustatory functions had returned to normal. A nasal endoscopy revealed some watery discharge in the posterior nasal cavity without any sign of other lesions. Follow-up tests for olfactory and gustatory functions were conducted, which showed improvement in both her scores.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Summary:
Sarah, a 40-year-old female, was admitted to the hospital with positive COVID-19 test results and mild symptoms of rhinorrhea, hyposmia, and ageusia. After receiving treatment, she was discharged from the hospital in stable condition. During her follow-up visit, her olfactory and gustatory functions had returned to normal without any further treatment. A nasal endoscopy showed no sign of lesions. Her overall prognosis is good.

text:
**Principal diagnosis code: U07.1 COVID-19, virus identified**

**Rationale**
- The patient was admitted with a positive COVID-19 test, so the virus was laboratory-confirmed. This is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. In ICD-10-AM (11th edition onward, and the Australian COVID-19 coding advice), U07.1 is used for confirmed cases.
- The rhinorrhea (R09.81 in ICD-10-CM; R09.88 in ICD-10-AM), hyposmia (R43.1 parosmia/R43.8 other disturbances of smell and taste) and ageusia (R43.2 parageusia/R43.8) are integral symptoms of COVID-19. They should not be coded separately as the principal diagnosis. Under ICD-10-AM, they could be listed as additional diagnoses only if they met the criteria for reporting, and here they are expected features of the disease.
- Pneumonia or other manifestations such as J12.82 are not documented, so no additional manifestation code is needed for the principal diagnosis.

**Notes**
- If this were an Australian-coded record, check for the current Australian Coding Standard (ACS 1202 for COVID-19 and ACS 0001 for the principal diagnosis) and any local updates to the coding advice.
- The follow-up Otolaryngology visit is a separate encounter and does not change the principal diagnosis for this admission.
- Hydroxychloroquine and azithromycin treatment does not require a separate diagnosis code.
